note: AI-drafted (Claude) multiple-choice items. Imported as status=draft, review_status=unreviewed: students never see them until a teacher approves them in Staff tools, which also publishes them.

items.prompt: My sister ___ two children.
items.explanation: Use 'has' with he/she/it in the present simple.

items.prompt: ___ you like coffee?
items.explanation: Questions in the present simple with 'you' use 'Do'.

items.prompt: This is Sara. ___ is my friend.
items.explanation: Use the subject pronoun 'She' for a woman or girl.

items.prompt: We ___ football on Fridays.
items.explanation: Use the base form of the verb with 'we' in the present simple.

items.prompt: That is ___ book. It belongs to me.
items.explanation: Use the possessive adjective 'my' before a noun.

items.prompt: He doesn't ___ meat.
items.explanation: After 'doesn't' use the base form of the verb.

items.prompt: Look! The children ___ in the garden.
items.explanation: Use the present continuous for actions happening now; 'children' is plural, so 'are'.

items.prompt: There ___ a cat under the table.
items.explanation: Use 'There is' with a singular noun.

items.prompt: I can ___ English.
items.explanation: After 'can' use the base form of the verb without 'to'.

items.prompt: The opposite of 'hot' is ___.
items.explanation: 'Cold' is the opposite of 'hot'.

items.prompt: I wake up in the ___ and go to bed at night.
items.explanation: We usually wake up in the morning.

items.prompt: My mother's brother is my ___.
items.explanation: Your parent's brother is your uncle.

items.prompt: You use a ___ to cut bread.
items.explanation: A knife is used for cutting.

items.prompt: Monday, Tuesday, ___, Thursday.
items.explanation: Wednesday comes between Tuesday and Thursday.

items.prompt: I'm ___. Can I have a glass of water?
items.explanation: When you need a drink, you are thirsty.

items.prompt: I ___ to the cinema last weekend.
items.explanation: 'Last weekend' is a finished time, so use the past simple 'went'.

items.prompt: Did you ___ the email I sent?
items.explanation: After 'Did' use the base form of the verb.

items.prompt: She was cooking when the phone ___.
items.explanation: A short action interrupting a longer one uses the past simple.

items.prompt: This bag is ___ than that one.
items.explanation: For adjectives ending in consonant + y, change y to i and add -er.

items.prompt: It's the ___ day of the year.
items.explanation: Superlative of 'hot': double the t and add -est.

items.prompt: I'm ___ visit my grandparents tomorrow.
items.explanation: Use 'be going to + verb' for plans.

items.prompt: You ___ wear a seatbelt in the car. It's the law.
items.explanation: 'Must' expresses an obligation such as a law.

items.prompt: How ___ sugar do you want in your tea?
items.explanation: 'Sugar' is uncountable, so use 'how much'.

items.prompt: We haven't got ___ milk left.
items.explanation: Use 'any' in negative sentences.

items.prompt: He usually ___ the bus to work.
items.explanation: Use the present simple for habits; 'he' takes -s.

items.prompt: I've lived here ___ 2019.
items.explanation: Use 'since' with a point in time.

items.prompt: She has worked here ___ five years.
items.explanation: Use 'for' with a period of time.

items.prompt: Have you ever ___ to Paris?
items.explanation: Present perfect: have + past participle 'been'.

items.prompt: The film was ___ boring that I fell asleep.
items.explanation: Use 'so + adjective + that' for a result.

items.prompt: I don't have ___ money to buy a car.
items.explanation: 'Enough' comes before a noun to mean 'as much as needed'.

items.prompt: If it rains, we ___ at home.
items.explanation: First conditional: if + present simple, will + verb.

items.prompt: The man ___ lives next door is a doctor.
items.explanation: Use 'who' for people in relative clauses.

items.prompt: She can't come because she ___ her leg.
items.explanation: Present perfect for a past action with a result now: has + broken.

items.prompt: We arrived ___ the airport at six o'clock.
items.explanation: 'Arrive at' is used for buildings and specific places like an airport.

items.prompt: My birthday is ___ June.
items.explanation: Use 'in' with months.

items.prompt: I need to ___ some money from the bank.
items.explanation: You withdraw money when you take it out of a bank account.

items.prompt: Can you ___ me your pen? I'll give it back.
items.explanation: You lend something to someone; they borrow it from you.

items.prompt: Please ___ off the lights when you leave.
items.explanation: 'Turn off' means to stop a light or machine working.

items.prompt: The train was ___, so it arrived an hour late.
items.explanation: 'Delayed' means later than planned.

items.prompt: He works in a hospital. He's a ___.
items.explanation: Nurses work in hospitals.

items.prompt: I always ___ my homework before dinner.
items.explanation: We say 'do homework'.

items.prompt: Don't ___ a noise. The baby is sleeping.
items.explanation: We say 'make a noise'.

items.prompt: It's raining. Take an ___.
items.explanation: An umbrella keeps you dry in the rain.

items.prompt: I'm looking ___ my keys. Have you seen them?
items.explanation: 'Look for' means try to find.

items.prompt: The shop is ___ on Sundays, so we can't go.
items.explanation: We can't go because it is not open.

items.prompt: If I ___ more time, I would learn to play the guitar.
items.explanation: Second conditional: if + past simple, would + verb.

items.prompt: The house ___ in 1920.
items.explanation: Passive voice in the past: was/were + past participle.

items.prompt: By the time we arrived, the film ___.
items.explanation: Past perfect shows an action completed before another past action.

items.prompt: She asked me where I ___.
items.explanation: In reported questions, use statement word order and backshift the tense.

items.prompt: I'm not used to ___ up so early.
items.explanation: 'Be used to' is followed by a noun or -ing form.

items.prompt: I used to ___ in London when I was a child.
items.explanation: 'Used to' is followed by the base form for past habits or states.

items.prompt: You ___ have told me earlier! Now it's too late.
items.explanation: 'Should have + past participle' criticises a past action that didn't happen.

items.prompt: I've been waiting here ___ two hours.
items.explanation: Use 'for' with a length of time.

items.prompt: He's the person ___ car was stolen.
items.explanation: 'Whose' shows possession in relative clauses.

items.prompt: She suggested ___ to the beach.
items.explanation: 'Suggest' is followed by the -ing form.

items.prompt: I decided ___ a new job.
items.explanation: 'Decide' is followed by 'to + infinitive'.

items.prompt: ___ it was raining, we went for a walk.
items.explanation: 'Although' is followed by a clause and shows contrast.

items.prompt: This time next week, I ___ on a beach.
items.explanation: Future continuous for an action in progress at a future time.

items.prompt: You don't need to bring food, ___?
items.explanation: A negative statement takes a positive question tag.

items.prompt: He told me that he ___ the report the day before.
items.explanation: In reported speech, past simple usually becomes past perfect.

items.prompt: The more you practise, the ___ you get.
items.explanation: 'The + comparative, the + comparative' structure.

items.prompt: I wish I ___ speak French.
items.explanation: 'Wish + past' (could) for present wishes about ability.

items.prompt: My car is being ___ at the moment.
items.explanation: Present continuous passive: is being + past participle.

items.prompt: Could you ___ after my dog while I'm away?
items.explanation: 'Look after' means take care of.

items.prompt: We had to ___ the meeting until next week.
items.explanation: 'Put off' means postpone.

items.prompt: She ___ an important decision yesterday.
items.explanation: We say 'make a decision'.

items.prompt: The museum is ___ visiting; it's fascinating.
items.explanation: 'Be worth + -ing' means it is good enough to do.

items.prompt: I can't ___ the noise from the street any more.
items.explanation: 'Can't stand' means cannot tolerate.

items.prompt: The company ___ 50 new employees to work in its new factory.
items.explanation: 'Hire' means give someone a job.

items.prompt: He was ___ of being late again, so he left early.
items.explanation: 'Afraid of + -ing' is the correct pattern; 'worried' takes 'about'.

items.prompt: She is very good ___ maths.
items.explanation: We say 'good at' a subject or activity.

items.prompt: I ___ my keys. I can't find them anywhere.
items.explanation: You 'lose' things you can't find; 'forget' is about memory.

items.prompt: The ___ of living in big cities is very high.
items.explanation: The fixed phrase is 'cost of living'.

items.prompt: He gave ___ smoking last year.
items.explanation: 'Give up' means stop doing a habit.

items.prompt: The weather ___ for tomorrow says it will be sunny.
items.explanation: 'Weather forecast' is the fixed phrase.

items.prompt: If I had known about the traffic, I ___ earlier.
items.explanation: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle.

items.prompt: Not only ___ late, but he also forgot the documents.
items.explanation: After a negative adverbial at the start, invert subject and auxiliary.

items.prompt: She must ___ the train; she isn't here yet.
items.explanation: 'Must have + past participle' expresses a logical deduction about the past.

items.prompt: I'd rather you ___ smoke in the house.
items.explanation: 'Would rather + subject + past simple' for preferences about others.

items.prompt: It's high time we ___ a decision.
items.explanation: 'It's (high) time + subject + past simple'.

items.prompt: By next June, I ___ here for ten years.
items.explanation: Future perfect for actions completed by a future time.

items.prompt: He is said ___ a fortune in the 1990s.
items.explanation: Passive reporting about the past: be said + to have + past participle.

items.prompt: I had my car ___ last week.
items.explanation: Causative: have + object + past participle.

items.prompt: ___ the bad weather, the match went ahead.
items.explanation: 'Despite' is followed by a noun phrase; 'in spite' needs 'of'.

items.prompt: Hardly had we sat down ___ the phone rang.
items.explanation: 'Hardly ... when' is the fixed pattern.

items.prompt: She regrets ___ him the truth.
items.explanation: 'Regret + -ing' refers to a past action you are sorry about.

items.prompt: Supposing you ___ the lottery, what would you do?
items.explanation: 'Supposing' works like 'if' in a second conditional: past simple.

items.prompt: The new policy will ___ effect from January.
items.explanation: The collocation is 'take effect'.

items.prompt: We need to ___ the problem before it gets worse.
items.explanation: 'Address a problem' means start dealing with it.

items.prompt: Her argument doesn't ___ water.
items.explanation: 'Not hold water' means not be convincing.

items.prompt: The manager ___ down the offer because the salary was too low.
items.explanation: 'Turn down' means refuse.

items.prompt: The results were ___ with our predictions.
items.explanation: 'Consistent with' means in agreement with.

items.prompt: Prices have risen ___ in the last year.
items.explanation: The natural collocation is 'rise sharply'.

items.prompt: I'll ___ into the matter and call you back.
items.explanation: 'Look into' means investigate.

items.prompt: The project was ___ by a lack of funding.
items.explanation: 'Hamper' means make progress difficult.

items.prompt: Had I realised the risks, I ___ the contract.
items.explanation: Inverted third conditional: Had + subject + past participle, would have + past participle.

items.prompt: Little ___ that the decision would change everything.
items.explanation: Negative adverbials like 'Little' at the start trigger inversion with an auxiliary.

items.prompt: The proposal, ___ was rejected, had taken months to prepare.
items.explanation: Non-defining relative clauses use 'which', not 'that'.

items.prompt: It is essential that every applicant ___ the form in person.
items.explanation: The subjunctive uses the base form after 'essential that'.

items.prompt: ___ to the press, the report would have caused a scandal.
items.explanation: An inverted past conditional matches 'would have caused'.

items.prompt: What I need ___ a long holiday.
items.explanation: In a 'What' cleft sentence, the 'What' clause is singular.

items.prompt: She would sooner resign ___ accept the new terms.
items.explanation: 'Would sooner ... than' expresses preference.

items.prompt: The minister's comments ___ a heated debate.
items.explanation: 'Spark a debate' means cause it to start.

items.prompt: The evidence ___ to the conclusion that the system had failed.
items.explanation: The pattern is 'point to a conclusion'; the others don't take 'to' here.

items.prompt: He tends to ___ the truth when it suits him.
items.explanation: 'Bend the truth' means say something not completely true.

items.prompt: The two studies reached ___ opposed conclusions.
items.explanation: 'Diametrically opposed' is a fixed collocation meaning completely opposite.

items.prompt: Her explanation ___ the issue rather than clarifying it.
items.explanation: 'Muddy the issue' means make it less clear, which contrasts with 'clarifying'.

items.prompt: The minister ___ the allegations as completely unfounded.
items.explanation: 'Dismiss something as ...' means reject it as not worth considering.

items.prompt: We must ___ a balance between cost and quality.
items.explanation: The collocation is 'strike a balance'.

items.prompt: The plan was abandoned because it was not financially ___.
items.explanation: 'Viable' means able to work successfully.

items.prompt: Under no circumstances ___ to leave the building.
items.explanation: 'Under no circumstances' at the start requires subject-auxiliary inversion.

items.prompt: So severe ___ that the road was closed for a week.
items.explanation: 'So + adjective' at the start triggers inversion: So severe was the damage...

items.prompt: Were the government ___ taxes, there would be protests.
items.explanation: Formal inverted conditional: Were + subject + to-infinitive.

items.prompt: Be that as it ___, we still need a decision today.
items.explanation: 'Be that as it may' is a fixed concessive expression.

items.prompt: Much ___ I admire her work, I can't agree with this.
items.explanation: 'Much as' means 'although' (Much as I admire...).

items.prompt: It was not until the 1990s ___ the theory was accepted.
items.explanation: Cleft pattern: 'It was not until ... that ...'.

items.prompt: His speech was full of ___ promises that nobody believed.
items.explanation: 'Hollow promises' are insincere ones.

items.prompt: The scandal ___ the party's chances of winning the election.
items.explanation: 'Scupper' means ruin a plan or chance.

items.prompt: She has a ___ for saying exactly the wrong thing.
items.explanation: 'Have a knack for' means have a natural tendency or skill.

items.prompt: The decision was taken ___, without consulting anyone.
items.explanation: 'Unilaterally' means by one side only, without others.

items.prompt: The author's style is ___: every word is carefully chosen.
items.explanation: 'Meticulous' means very careful and precise.

items.prompt: The two accounts of the event are ___; they cannot both be true.
items.explanation: 'Irreconcilable' means impossible to make compatible.

items.prompt: Critics were quick to ___ holes in the argument.
items.explanation: 'Pick holes in' means find faults in.

items.prompt: The negotiations reached an ___, with neither side willing to compromise.
items.explanation: An 'impasse' is a situation where no progress is possible.

items.prompt: His ___ remarks offended almost everyone in the room.
items.explanation: 'Tactless' means not sensitive to others' feelings.
